bib.title: Promptagator: Few-shot Dense Retrieval From 8 Examples
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v1; ICLR 2023 not in PDF text)

question: Can a handful (<=8) of task-specific examples, amplified by an LLM query generator, produce task-specific dense retrievers that beat retrievers trained on large supervised sets such as MS MARCO?
hypothesis: Different retrieval tasks have different search intents and query distributions, so retrievers trained from one or two QA datasets generalise poorly; task-specific prompting can supply the missing intent.
contributions: Analyse differences in search intent and query distribution across retrieval tasks and propose a Few-Shot Retrieval setting for BEIR
Propose PROMPTAGATOR, a recipe for few-shot retrieval using LLM-generated task-specific training data
Show 2-8 examples give retrievers better than recent models trained on MS MARCO or NQ with over 500K labels, and reranking adds about 5 points

method.summary: A task description plus up to 8 query-document examples prompts FLAN 137B to write queries for up to 1M corpus documents; a dual encoder trained on those pairs filters them by round-trip consistency (keep a pair only if the document is ranked top-1) and is fine-tuned again on the survivors. A 110M cross-attention reranker (PROMPTAGATOR++) is trained on the same synthetic data.

datasets.name: BEIR (11 public datasets: ArguAna, Touche-2020, TREC-Covid, NFCorpus, HotpotQA, DBPedia-Entity, Climate-FEVER, FEVER, SciFact, SCIDOCS, FiQA)
datasets.split: test; few-shot examples (2 to 8) sampled from dev when available, otherwise from test and counted as 'failed to retrieve'
datasets.preprocessing: MS MARCO, NQ and Quora excluded from main evaluation; Climate-FEVER excluded from some comparisons via FEVER prompt (24.0*, not in average)

datasets.name: Synthetic (query, document) pairs
datasets.size: up to 1M documents per corpus x 8 queries; total 29.23M queries x 2 prompts = 58.46M queries, 610M words
datasets.preprocessing: Outputs lacking the query description are dropped; examples reduced/truncated to FLAN input limit

datasets.name: C4
datasets.source: retriever pretraining with Contriever independent cropping

datasets.name: MS MARCO
datasets.split: used as validation set to tune K; also Fig 2b comparison vs supervised data

models.name: FLAN (137B)
models.architecture: instruction-tuned LM, same pretrained model as LaMDA

other.note: Original FLAN training overlapped NQ and Quora; an extra FLAN trained without them was ablated

models.name: PROMPTAGATOR dual encoder
models.architecture: shared T5-base v1.1 encoder, mean pooling of top layer, 768-dim embedding (GTR recipe)
models.init_from: T5 checkpoint, then pretrained on C4

training.objective: cross-entropy over in-batch random negatives (dual encoder); cross-entropy with 31 sampled negatives from top 200 retrieved passages (reranker)
training.batch_size: dual encoder: 128 for small corpora (<50k docs), 6k for others; reranker: 64 for all
training.steps: dual encoder: 5k for large corpora (>500k), 1k for others; reranker: 20k for large, 5k for others
training.epochs: 'a set number of epochs' before filtering (not stated)
training.compute: query generation: 58.46M queries, 610M words with FLAN 137B; no training compute given

other.stages: C4 independent-cropping pretrain, fine-tune on synthetic pairs, filter with initial encoder, continue fine-tuning on filtered data

inference.samples: 8 queries per document; single run per config, no seeds reported
inference.prompting: instruction prompt (edoc(d1), equery(q1), ..., edoc(dk), equery(qk), edoc(d)) with k<=8 task examples; zero-shot uses one universal prompt

parameters.K (round-trip filter): 1, tuned on MS MARCO, used for all BEIR datasets
parameters.examples per prompt: at most 8, fewer if over FLAN input limit (Fig 4: 3 to 8 depending on dataset)

eval.protocol: nDCG@10 on 11 BEIR test sets, average over datasets; few-shot examples from test counted as failed; single run, no significance test or seeds reported

availability.code: not stated; prompts and few-shot examples promised to be released

prompts.text: {d} Read the passage and generate a query.

evidence.quote: we use 128 batch size for small datasets and 6k for others

results.claim: Few-shot PROMPTAGATOR (110M dual encoder) averages 47.8 nDCG@10 on 11 BEIR datasets, above BM25.
results.setup: 11 BEIR datasets (excl. MS MARCO, NQ, Quora), few-shot 2-8 examples per task, FLAN 137B query generation, 110M T5-base dual encoder
results.table: Table 2, row PROMPTAGATOR (110M) Few-shot, column AVG.

results.claim: Few-shot PROMPTAGATOR beats SPLADE v2 and ColBERT v2, which use token-level interaction and distillation.
results.setup: 11 BEIR datasets (excl. MS MARCO, NQ, Quora), few-shot 2-8 examples per task, FLAN 137B query generation, 110M T5-base dual encoder
results.note: Abstract says ColBERT v2 beaten by more than 1.2 nDCG.
results.table: Table 2, rows SPLADE v2 (46.6) and ColBERT v2 (46.2), column AVG.

results.claim: Zero-shot PROMPTAGATOR averages 45.5, near MS MARCO-supervised retrievers.
results.setup: Universal prompt 'Read the passage and generate a query.', 11 BEIR datasets

results.claim: PROMPTAGATOR++ few-shot (110M+110M reranker) reaches 52.8, about 5 points above the retriever.
results.setup: Reranks top 200 from PROMPTAGATOR; 11 BEIR datasets
results.table: Table 2, row PROMPTAGATOR++ Few-shot, column AVG.
Table 2, row PROMPTAGATOR++ Zero-shot, column AVG.

results.claim: Round-trip filtering improves 8 of 11 datasets and gives +2.5 points on average.
results.setup: Few-shot PROMPTAGATOR with vs without filter (Fig 2a)
results.quote: ﬁltering improves performance on 8 out of 11 datasets, and leads to 2.5 points improvement on average

results.claim: Filtering hurt NFCorpus and SciFact, the smallest datasets in generated queries; authors conjecture overfitting.
results.quote: There are nonetheless datasets where ﬁltering hurts model quality such as NFCorpus and SciFact.

results.claim: Eight examples plus the LLM match about 50k labelled MS MARCO examples for a simple dual encoder.
results.setup: MS MARCO, dual encoder only, no other components; read from Fig 2b caption
results.quote: making 8 examples to catch up with 50k labeled examples, when simple dual encoders are used

results.claim: Biggest gains over baselines are on Touche-2020 then ArguAna; few-shot Touche 34.5 vs BM25 36.7 is not above BM25.
results.note: Text says biggest improvement is on Touche over baselines; BM25 scores 36.7 there, higher than 34.5. Gain is relative to the other neural baselines.
results.table: Table 2, row PROMPTAGATOR Few-shot, column touché
Table 2, row PROMPTAGATOR Few-shot, column arg

results.claim: Climate-FEVER is the one dataset where few-shot (16.8) is below zero-shot (21.4); with the FEVER prompt it scores 24.0.
results.setup: Climate-FEVER, BEIR pairs include 'not enough info' as relevant
results.note: 24.0* uses FEVER prompt and is not in the average.
results.table: Table 2, row PROMPTAGATOR Few-shot, column climate (16.8 (24.0*)); Zero-shot 21.4

results.claim: Zero-shot PROMPTAGATOR beats NQ-QGen and GenQ query generators by large margins with the same filtering and training recipe.
results.quote: These results indicate that the main contributing factor to PROMPTAGATOR is the prompted LLM query generation, not the speciﬁc training recipe or hype-parameters.

results.claim: Removing NQ and Quora from FLAN training drops the few-shot average from 48.5 to 47.0, still above prior retrievers.
results.setup: Table 3, FLAN w/o NQ and Quora, retriever
results.note: FLAN original AVG is 48.5 in Table 3 but 47.8 in Table 2; Table 3 uses the Fever model for Climate-FEVER and appears to include it in the average.
results.table: Table 3, row FLAN w/o NQ and Quora, column AVG.

results.claim: Generation cost: 29.23M queries x 2 prompts = 58.46M queries, 610M words.
results.setup: FLAN 137B query generation for all datasets
results.quote: we generated 29.23M queries * 2 prompts = 58.46M queries, for a total of 610M words

results.claim: Average generated query length: few-shot 17.8 words, zero-shot 13.5, NQ-QGen 9.6; ArguAna few-shot 98.2.

limits: Authors: data efficiency unexplored (how many generated pairs are needed per task).
Authors: sensitivity to the prompt not studied.
Query-specific K could retain good pairs removed by the K=1 filter (left to future work).
Filtering hurt the smallest datasets (possible overfitting).
FLAN training overlapped NQ and Quora; ablation shows small drop only.
Single runs, no seeds or significance tests, no optimizer or learning rate reported; FLAN 137B is not public (checkpoint 'provided by the authors').
Generation cost is expensive (distillation of a 137B LLM); no wall-clock or hardware stated.

terms.definition: each task comes with a short description and a few annotated examples
a query should be answered by the passage from which the query was generated
